Aside from the issues pointed out in this thread already, my concern is mainly "What happens to games that are sold outside Steam"? First and foremost, publishers are given an incentive to lock down versions of their game sold outside Steam further to deter would-be modders from creating mods that game developers don't get a cut of, which in turn essentially gimps games sold outside Steam, giving Steam an unfair advantage over other retailers.

Devs lock down modding tools because the mods compete with their own sequels. Civilization 4 for example was arguably better than Civilization 5 because the modding capabilities were much greater. A popular Civ4 mod even managed to form its own spinoff product. or Elemental: Fallen Enchantress.

Who is the creator in this case?

There are VERY few mods out there that do not build upon scripts and assets made by others.

The gaming community is slowly being nickle and dimed for everything, and a lot of people are sick of it. Mods use to be a bonus for PC games because they could extend the life of a game.
